bounds.domain: Two opaque thread identities (TLC symbols 1 and 2); the actual Android hook uses native 64-bit IDs 1 and 4294967296 with the same 32-bit hash. One queued read and two unique native-notice receipt generations per selected conversation. Incoming publication and reads share the existing serial worker. Native receipt uniqueness and successful notification publication are premises; no UUID collision proof or fairness/provider-success assumption is made for safety.
bounds.conformance: Six exact Android JVM cases exercise actual notification/PendingIntent identities, MessagingStyle retained text, compose-only reply, the actual receiver and its completion future, and actual SQL provider update predicates for shown/later/foreign/sent rows, role loss and partial provider failure. A real held-worker incoming-before-old-tap case checks that even a new backdated row remains unread and its newer notice remains visible. Current-action retry and replaced/successful PendingIntent retirement are mandatory.
bounds.limits: Read predicates are abstracted to selected-thread membership; timestamp units/cutoffs are checked by actual SQLite tests. Separate provider writes can partially succeed. Real default-SMS role grants, system Telephony provider enforcement, carrier delivery, audio/video, system notification rendering and process death remain external. Reply never invokes the send journal or radio. Other callers of the timestamp-based markThreadRead API retain their own view-selection contract. Failed or ambiguous native NotificationManager publication/cancellation is outside this finite normal-return projection. Timestamp predicates approximate membership for external or backdated provider changes outside these serial incoming paths; no complete provider-row snapshot or external-writer exclusion is proved.

assumptions: Weak fairness of the admitted worker and return of each provider update with success or failure. This assumes finite provider calls, not successful writes or carrier delivery.
No fairness. An admitted worker, external query or posted Main continuation can remain stalled indefinitely.
